points.description: Final answer: steady-state θss = 0.800 (rad, i.e. b·Nff/(c+b·k1) = 0.75×8/(6+0.75×2) = 6/7.5) AND the tracking error stated as 20% (θ is 20% below the reference, i.e. −20%). Uses Nff = 8, k1 = 2 from part (a). Sign convention may be either as long as it is clear that the output falls short by 20%.

levels.says: Correct θss = 0.8 but percentage error missing or wrong, or correct 20% error stated without θss value.

points.description: Explanation: Nff is a feedforward gain on the reference path, outside the feedback loop, so feedback (k1θ, k2θ̇) cannot correct the DC calibration error. No integrator or error-driven correction exists, so the steady-state gain inherits the actuator gain error. Merely saying 'gain changed' without reference to feedforward being outside the feedback path earns no credit.

rubric.notes: Full marks: θss = 0.800 with error 20% below reference, plus an explanation that Nff lies outside the feedback path so the gain error is uncorrected. Part marks on P1 if only one of the number or percentage is correct. An explanation that does not mention feedforward being outside the loop earns nothing on P2.
rubric.answer_key: At steady state θ̇=θ̈=0: cθ = b(Nff r − k1θ) ⇒ θss = b Nff r/(c + b k1). From part (a) with b=1 and θss=r: Nff = c + k1 = 8, k1 = 2. With b=0.75: θss = 0.75×8/(6+1.5) = 6/7.5 = 0.800. Error = (0.8−1)/1 = −20%. Cause: Nff is feedforward outside the feedback loop, so feedback cannot correct it; no integrator. Final answer: θss = 0.800 (error −20%).
